# vk 0.13.4 — Publication predicate and selection-loop trimming

Development release, 2026-11-22. Cargo package **`vkrust 0.13.4+1.4.365`**,
Rust library/import name **`vk`**, Git tag **`v0.13.4`**, MIT licensed.
The Vulkan header snapshot remains 1.4.365; it is not a minimum driver version.
Public function names, signatures and error payloads are unchanged.

## Allocator changes

Publication evaluated margin-guard eligibility twice per operation — two
`memory_flags` probes and two guard-capability checks producing the
`guard_size`/`guard_offset` pair. The predicate now computes once and both
values derive from it. The memory-type selection loop previously re-read
`required_flags`, `preferred_flags`, the avoided mask and the per-type heap
record on every admitted-bit iteration; the raw masks and heap record are now
loaded once. Required/rejected-flag, tile-memory, AMD device-coherent,
protected and heap-size decisions keep their existing order and increasing-
index tie behavior. Error order is unchanged.

## Measured results

The complete [Surface Laptop 5 report](../benchmarks/surface-laptop-5-2026-11-22.md)
retains the committed-tree matrix, both backend build identities, kept and
rejected experiments and validation runs.

On the latest matrix (20 fresh-process samples per cell, unlocked clocks,
shared workstation): **23 of 44 combined workloads complete below 1.0× VMA**,
including every virtual-placement row (0.629–0.894), pooled-buffer
reverse/FIFO (0.951–0.965), single-buffer pooled lifetimes (0.904) and newly
separate-buffer reverse (0.975). Native cells span 0.904–1.100; the worst
measured gap is separate-buffer churn at 1.100. Mapping cycles are
0.998–1.037×. Separate-buffer and image churn retain the largest residual in
their create phase — duplicate-handle detection and association bookkeeping
that VMA does not perform. The below-0.9× target across the suite is not met.

## Correctness

All 44 benchmark cells pass under separate core and synchronization
validation on the committed tree. The 3,463-test workspace suite, including
54 native `mem` tests, passes on the recorded device. Strict library Clippy,
formatting and `git diff --check` pass. These results qualify the named
workloads on this machine, not Vulkan conformance, other devices/drivers or
the full feature set.
